context.analysis:
## Overview
[An Amazon-style global e-commerce platform for purchasing physical and electronic books, supporting multi-currency transactions, recommendations, and reviews.]

## Key Elements
* Customer (Book Buyer)
* Site Administrator / Content Moderator
* Online Bookstore System (AWS multi-region)
* Third-Party Shipping Partner
* Payment Gateway (Stripe/PayPal)
* Tax & Currency Service
* Third-Party Identity Provider (Google/Apple OAuth 2.0 / OIDC)
* Notification Service (AWS SES / SendGrid)

## Relationships
* Customer -> Online Bookstore System: Browses, buys, reviews [HTTPS]
* Site Administrator -> Online Bookstore System: Manages catalog and moderates [HTTPS]
* Customer -> Third-Party Identity Provider: Authenticates [OIDC / OAuth 2.0]
* Online Bookstore System -> Third-Party Identity Provider: Validates tokens [HTTPS]
* Online Bookstore System -> Payment Gateway: Processes transactions [HTTPS / REST / TLS 1.3]
* Online Bookstore System -> Third-Party Shipping Partner: Sends fulfillment orders [HTTPS / REST]
* Online Bookstore System -> Notification Service: Dispatches transactional emails [HTTPS / REST / AWS SQS]

## Technology Stack
* AWS Cloud Provider: Ensures 99.95% availability across regions (us-east-1, eu-west-1, ap-southeast-1).
* TLS 1.3: Mandated for all external interactions and secure data in transit.
* AES-256: Used for data encryption at rest to satisfy GDPR and CCPA compliance.
* AWS SQS: Asynchronous message queuing for notifications to prevent checkout latency.
* OAuth 2.0 / OIDC: Used via external IdPs to streamline customer authentication.

## Rationale
[The architecture uses cloud-native multi-region deployment and asynchronous processing to guarantee scalability, performance, and 99.95% uptime. Security controls and externalized services ensure compliance while optimizing user conversion rates.]

containers.analysis:
## Overview
The Online Bookstore is a scaled-down e-commerce platform built on AWS for selling physical and electronic books, supporting 1 million monthly active users across multiple global regions. It provides catalog browsing, secure checkout, reviews, and personalized recommendations while ensuring strict compliance with GDPR, CCPA, and OWASP security standards.

## Key Elements
* **Users**: Customer, Site Administrator
* **Frontend**: Single Page App (React / TypeScript) hosted on AWS S3 & CloudFront
* **Gateway**: AWS API Gateway
* **Microservices**: Catalog & Search, Order & Checkout, Recommendation, Content Management / Moderation, Notification
* **Data Stores**: AWS Aurora PostgreSQL, AWS DynamoDB
* **Integration Services**: AWS SQS, AWS EventBridge, AWS App Mesh, AWS Secrets Manager, AWS KMS
* **External Systems**: Third-Party Shipping Partner, Payment Gateway, Tax & Currency Service, Third-Party Identity Provider, Notification Service

## Relationships
* **Customer to SPA**: HTTPS over TLS 1.3
* **SPA to API Gateway**: HTTPS/JSON REST APIs
* **API Gateway to Microservices**: gRPC over mTLS via AWS App Mesh
* **Microservices to Data Stores**: TCP with AWS KMS encryption at rest
* **Order & Checkout to Payment Gateway**: HTTPS REST API
* **Order & Checkout to Shipping Partner**: HTTPS API

## Technology Stack
* **Frontend**: React, TypeScript (For responsive user interface)
* **Backend Runtime**: Spring Boot for Java (Catalog), Node.js with TypeScript (Order, Notification), FastAPI with Python (Recommendations)
* **Search & Compute**: AWS OpenSearch (Sub-2s keyword search), AWS ECS Fargate (Container hosting)
* **Messaging & Events**: AWS SQS, AWS EventBridge / MSK Kafka (Asynchronous decoupling)
* **Security & Infrastructure**: AWS IAM, AWS Secrets Manager, AWS WAF, AWS KMS (Compliance and secrets injection)

## Rationale
This multi-region AWS microservices architecture isolates PCI-DSS and GDPR data scopes while ensuring 99.95% availability and sub-2-second page loads. Decoupled containers using gRPC over mTLS and asynchronous SQS messaging guarantee scalability for 1M MAU without performance degradation.

Single Page App.analysis:
## Overview
[The Online Bookstore Single Page App provides a responsive user interface for catalog browsing, secure checkout, reviews, and recommendations. It is built to support 1 million monthly active users globally while ensuring low-latency performance and strict security compliance.]

## Key Elements
* Single Page App (React, TypeScript, AWS S3, AWS CloudFront)
* Routing & State Manager (React Router, Redux Toolkit / React Context)
* Catalog & Search UI Module
* Checkout & Cart UI Module
* Recommendation & Review UI Module
* Analytics & Telemetry Module
* Resilience & Storage Manager (IndexedDB)
* API Gateway (AWS API Gateway)

## Relationships
* Customer -> Single Page App [HTTPS over TLS 1.3]
* Site Administrator -> Single Page App [HTTPS over TLS 1.3]
* Single Page App -> API Gateway [HTTPS/JSON REST APIs]
* Single Page App Components -> Single Page App (Internal runtime communication via React props/context)

## Technology Stack
* React & TypeScript: Delivers dynamic, type-safe client-side UI components and modular architecture.
* AWS S3 & AWS CloudFront: Hosts static assets globally and enforces TLS 1.3 with HSTS and CSP headers.
* React Router & Redux Toolkit: Manages client-side navigation, global session state, and shopping cart persistence.
* IndexedDB: Provides local browser storage for offline cart persistence during degraded network conditions.
* Payment Gateway SDK: Handles secure, tokenized checkout to maintain zero PCI-DSS exposure in the SPA.

## Rationale
[This component architecture ensures sub-2-second page loads on 3G networks globally by leveraging static edge caching via CloudFront and efficient client-side rendering with React. It enforces robust security and privacy compliance (GDPR, CCPA, OWASP Top-10) by eliminating local token storage, sanitizing analytics data, and isolating sensitive checkout operations.]

API Gateway.analysis:
## Overview
[The API Gateway component securely routes, throttles, and translates incoming client requests for the Online Bookstore microservices architecture. It provides edge security, authentication, and telemetry while ensuring compliance with performance and privacy standards.]

## Key Elements
[
• Edge Router & SSL Termination (AWS WAF & CloudFront)
• Authentication & Authorization Authorizer (AWS Lambda Custom Authorizer)
• Rate Limiting & Throttling Engine (AWS API Gateway Usage Plans)
• Service Proxy & Protocol Translator (AWS API Gateway & AWS App Mesh)
• Usage & Analytics Logging (AWS CloudWatch & Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose)
]

## Relationships
[
• Single Page App -> Edge Router: Sends secure client traffic [HTTPS/JSON REST APIs]
• Authentication Authorizer -> Third-Party Identity Provider: Validates user tokens [HTTPS]
• Service Proxy -> Backend Microservices: Routes internal calls with App Mesh [gRPC over mTLS]
• API Gateway -> Usage & Analytics Logging: Streams sanitized access telemetry [CloudWatch Logs / Kinesis]
]

## Technology Stack
[
• AWS API Gateway: Managed entry point for high scalability and built-in throttling
• AWS WAF & CloudFront: Edge protection against OWASP Top-10 threats and global routing
• AWS Lambda: Executes stateless custom authorization and token validation
• AWS App Mesh: Manages zero-trust service-to-service gRPC communication
• Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose: Asynchronously streams sanitized logs for analytics without impacting latency
]

## Rationale
[This component architecture guarantees high availability (99.95%) and strict performance limits (<2s page load) by offloading edge security, rate limiting, and analytics. It ensures regional routing and robust GDPR/CCPA compliance via PII masking and zero-trust internal transport.]

Catalog & Search Microservice.analysis:
## Overview
The Catalog & Search Microservice is a core revenue-driving Spring Boot application providing sub-2-second faceted search, real-time inventory visibility, and administrative catalog management. It utilizes a CQRS pattern to isolate high-throughput search traffic from write operations while maintaining GDPR and CCPA compliance.

## Key Elements
- `SearchController`: Spring MVC component exposing gRPC endpoints for keyword and faceted searches.
- `CatalogQueryService`: Spring Service orchestrating queries against AWS OpenSearch.
- `CatalogAdminController`: Spring MVC component handling administrative mutations with strict RBAC.
- `CatalogRepository`: Spring Data JPA component managing writes and reads against AWS Aurora PostgreSQL.
- `InventoryConsumer`: Spring Kafka consumer processing asynchronous inventory updates.
- `SearchAnalyticsService`: Component capturing anonymous search telemetry asynchronously.
- AWS OpenSearch: Managed search engine for typo-tolerant full-text search.
- AWS Aurora PostgreSQL: Relational database for canonical book metadata.
- AWS MSK (Kafka): Event streaming platform for domain events (`catalog.updated`).

## Relationships
- API Gateway -> `SearchController`: Routes search and catalog requests via gRPC over mTLS.
- API Gateway -> `CatalogAdminController`: Routes administrative mutations via gRPC over mTLS with JWT validation.
- `CatalogQueryService` -> AWS OpenSearch: Queries catalog data via REST over HTTPS with TLS.
- `CatalogRepository` -> AWS Aurora PostgreSQL: Reads and writes canonical data via JDBC with AWS KMS encryption at rest.
- `InventoryConsumer` -> AWS MSK (Kafka): Consumes inventory update events via AMQP/Kafka.
- `CatalogAdminController` -> `CatalogRepository`: Writes metadata via JDBC.
- `CatalogAdminController` -> AWS MSK (Kafka): Emits `catalog.updated` domain events secured with AWS KMS.
- `SearchAnalyticsService`: Publishes anonymous telemetry asynchronously.

## Technology Stack
- Java 17 / Spring Boot: Core framework chosen for enterprise robustness and robust dependency injection.
- Spring MVC / gRPC: Protocol chosen for high-performance inter-container communication.
- AWS OpenSearch: Selected for scalable, typo-tolerant full-text search and faceted filtering.
- AWS Aurora PostgreSQL: Chosen for reliable, transactional storage of canonical book metadata.
- AWS MSK (Kafka): Selected for asynchronous, decoupled event-driven communication and CQRS synchronization.
- AWS ECS Fargate: Chosen for serverless container orchestration meeting 99.95% availability targets.
- AWS KMS: Utilized for data encryption at rest and message integrity protection.

## Rationale
The CQRS pattern separates read-heavy search operations from administrative writes, ensuring sub-2-second performance on 3G networks and supporting 1M MAU. Zero-trust networking protocols (mTLS, TLS to OpenSearch, and AWS KMS) satisfy stringent GDPR, CCPA, and OWASP Top-10 security constraints.

Order & Checkout Microservice.analysis:
## Overview
The Order & Checkout Microservice processes customer financial transactions, multi-currency pricing, and shipping integrations for the Online Bookstore. It ensures secure, distributed transaction orchestration while maintaining GDPR and PCI-DSS compliance.

## Key Elements
- **Shopper & Customer Support Agent**: Internal actors interacting with the checkout and order management flows.
- **Order API Controller**: Handles incoming gRPC requests and JWT-based authorization.
- **Checkout Orchestrator (Saga Coordinator)**: Manages distributed transaction workflows and transient failures.
- **Payment Processor Client**: Integrates with the Payment Gateway using tokenization.
- **Fulfillment Adapter**: Interfaces with the Third-Party Shipping Partner API.
- **Tax & Currency Evaluator**: Handles real-time USD, EUR, and GBP conversion.
- **Retry & DLQ Manager**: Manages asynchronous failure resilience.
- **Event Publisher**: Dispatches domain events to downstream services.
- **Order Repository**: Persists encrypted transaction and order data.

## Relationships
- **API Gateway -> Order API Controller**: Routes incoming checkout requests [gRPC over mTLS via AWS App Mesh]
- **Checkout Orchestrator -> Payment Processor Client**: Processes financial transactions [HTTPS REST API]
- **Checkout Orchestrator -> Fulfillment Adapter**: Sends fulfillment data [HTTPS API]
- **Checkout Orchestrator -> Tax & Currency Evaluator**: Fetches localized pricing [HTTPS REST]
- **Checkout Orchestrator -> Retry & DLQ Manager**: Offloads transient failures [AWS SQS with AWS KMS]
- **Event Publisher -> Notification Microservice**: Dispatches order state changes [AWS EventBridge / SNS]
- **Order Repository -> AWS Aurora PostgreSQL**: Persists order data [TCP with AWS KMS encryption at rest]

## Technology Stack
- **Node.js & TypeScript**: Core runtime and language for business logic execution.
- **AWS ECS Fargate**: Container orchestration platform for serverless compute.
- **AWS Aurora PostgreSQL & TypeORM**: Relational data store enforcing field-level encryption for PII.
- **AWS SQS**: Asynchronous messaging for retry queues and dead-letter handling.
- **AWS EventBridge / SNS**: Event-driven communication backbone for domain notifications.
- **AWS KMS**: Cryptographic service ensuring encryption at rest for databases and queues.

## Rationale
This component architecture uses a Saga pattern with a dedicated orchestrator and DLQ management to ensure high availability and prevent transaction loss during third-party outages. Strict data minimization and tokenization isolate sensitive PII and financial records to guarantee GDPR and PCI-DSS compliance.

Recommendation Microservice.analysis:
## Overview
The Online Bookstore Recommendation Microservice provides personalized and fallback book recommendations to drive customer engagement. It is architected for high scalability, fault tolerance, and GDPR/CCPA compliance.

## Key Elements
- **Customer**: End-user browsing the e-commerce platform and receiving recommendations.
- **API Router Layer**: FastAPI application managing incoming gRPC requests and input validation via Pydantic.
- **Inference Engine Component**: Executes collaborative filtering and incorporates a Cold-Start Handling Component for fallback trending logic.
- **Recommendation Cache**: AWS ElastiCache Redis cluster for sub-10ms cached retrieval of precomputed suggestions.
- **Data Sync Worker**: Asynchronous background worker processing order events.
- **Database**: AWS DynamoDB storing vector embeddings and model weights encrypted with AWS KMS.

## Relationships
- **API Gateway -> API Router Layer**: Routes recommendation requests via gRPC over mTLS using AWS App Mesh.
- **API Router Layer -> Inference Engine**: Delegates request handling via in-memory Python function calls.
- **Inference Engine -> Recommendation Cache**: Fetches precomputed recommendations via TCP/Redis Protocol with TLS-in-transit.
- **Inference Engine -> Database**: Executes fallback reads for sparse user profiles via HTTPS using AWS SDK.
- **Data Sync Worker -> Database**: Persists updated model weights and embeddings via HTTPS using AWS SDK.
- **AWS EventBridge/SQS -> Data Sync Worker**: Consumes order events asynchronously.

## Technology Stack
- **Python / FastAPI**: Chosen for robust machine learning library integration and high-performance asynchronous routing.
- **AWS ECS Fargate**: Serverless container orchestration ensuring zero-infrastructure management and auto-scaling.
- **AWS ElastiCache Redis**: In-memory caching layer providing sub-10ms response times.
- **AWS DynamoDB**: Scalable NoSQL storage for vector embeddings with AWS KMS encryption at rest.
- **Pydantic**: Built-in FastAPI validation ensuring strict input parsing for OWASP Top-10 mitigation.

## Rationale
The architecture decouples real-time inference from heavy batch processing using caching and asynchronous event workers to guarantee sub-200ms responses and 99.95% uptime for 1M MAU. Granular IAM roles, PII pseudonymization, and secure VPC protocols ensure strict adherence to GDPR and CCPA compliance requirements.

Content Management & Moderation Microser.analysis:
## Overview
[The Content Management & Moderation Microservice manages user-generated reviews, ratings, and content moderation workflows for the Online Bookstore. It ensures strict GDPR/CCPA compliance, OWASP Top-10 security mitigations, and automated user feedback loops.]

## Key Elements
- **Review & Rating Controller**: Node.js/TypeScript REST/gRPC endpoints handling customer review submissions, updates, and GDPR erasure requests.
- **Moderation Workflow Engine**: Manages queue states and enforces RBAC/ABAC authorization for Site Administrators and Customers.
- **Content Sanitizer Component**: DOMPurify-based input validation layer mitigating XSS and injection vulnerabilities.
- **Data Access Repository**: Interfaces with AWS Aurora PostgreSQL for secure multi-tenant storage.
- **Notification Dispatcher Component**: Asynchronous integration layer publishing moderation events.

## Relationships
- **API Gateway -> Review & Rating Controller / Moderation Workflow Engine**: Routes moderation requests via gRPC over mTLS through AWS App Mesh.
- **Review & Rating Controller & Moderation Workflow Engine -> Data Access Repository**: Reads and writes data via secure TCP with AWS KMS encryption.
- **Notification Dispatcher Component -> Notification Microservice**: Publishes moderation events asynchronously via AWS EventBridge over HTTPS with IAM authentication.

## Technology Stack
- **Runtime**: Node.js with TypeScript for application logic and microservice containers.
- **Compute**: AWS ECS Fargate for scalable, serverless container orchestration.
- **Sanitization**: DOMPurify for robust input validation and XSS mitigation.
- **Messaging**: AWS EventBridge for decoupled asynchronous event publishing.
- **Security & Encryption**: AWS KMS for column-level and data-at-rest encryption, TLS 1.3 for transit security.

## Rationale
[This architecture uses containerized Node.js microservices on AWS ECS Fargate to scale effortlessly and meet strict 99.95% availability targets. Integrated compliance controls, including DOMPurify, AWS KMS encryption, and AWS EventBridge pseudonymization, ensure full GDPR/CCPA adherence without sacrificing system performance.]

Notification Microservice.analysis:
## Overview
[The Notification Microservice handles asynchronous user messaging, preference management, and promotional broadcasts for the Online Bookstore. It ensures GDPR/CCPA compliance and 99.95% uptime while dispatching transactional and marketing communications.]

## Key Elements
- End Customer
- Marketing/Admin User
- Notification Microservice (Node.js, TypeScript, AWS ECS Fargate)
- Event Consumer / Message Broker Listener (Node.js, AWS SQS SDK)
- Notification Router & Template Engine (Node.js, Handlebars)
- Channel Adapters (Node.js, AWS SES, AWS SNS, FCM SDKs)
- Preference Controller (Express.js, TypeScript)
- Notification DB (AWS DynamoDB, AWS KMS)
- Campaign Manager Component (Express.js, TypeScript)
- Webhook Receiver Component (Express.js, TypeScript)

## Relationships
- API Gateway -> Preference Controller: Routes preference requests [gRPC over mTLS via AWS App Mesh]
- API Gateway -> Campaign Manager: Routes admin broadcast requests [REST over HTTPS]
- Event Consumer -> Notification Router: Dispatches messages [Internal function call]
- Campaign Manager -> Notification Router: Dispatches bulk payload batches [Internal function call]
- Preference Controller -> Notification DB: Reads and writes user consent [TCP]
- AWS SES/SNS -> Webhook Receiver: Delivers engagement callbacks [HTTPS]
- Channel Adapters -> AWS SES / SNS / FCM: Dispatches notifications [HTTPS REST / AWS SQS]

## Technology Stack
- Node.js & TypeScript: Core runtime and language for the microservice ensuring type safety and scalability.
- AWS ECS Fargate: Serverless container orchestration for reliable microservice deployment.
- AWS DynamoDB & AWS KMS: NoSQL storage with customer-managed keys for secure, compliant data persistence.
- Handlebars: Templating engine for localized message rendering.
- Express.js: Web framework for REST endpoints and webhook handling.

## Rationale
[The component decomposition cleanly separates transactional messaging, campaign management, and user consent into distinct modules within a secure Node.js container. Leveraging AWS serverless and managed security services guarantees strict GDPR/CCPA compliance, robust RBAC, and high availability.]

Database.analysis:
## Overview
The Online Bookstore system uses a polyglot persistence strategy with AWS Aurora PostgreSQL and AWS DynamoDB to support high-throughput e-commerce operations. It ensures multi-region scalability, strict GDPR/CCPA compliance, and secure data isolation.

## Key Elements
* Transactional Data Store (AWS Aurora PostgreSQL Multi-AZ with Primary Writer and Read-Replica Cluster)
* NoSQL Data Store (AWS DynamoDB)
* Key Management Component (AWS KMS)
* Microservices (Catalog & Search, Order & Checkout, Recommendation, Content Management)

## Relationships
* Catalog & Search Microservice -> Aurora Read-Replica Cluster: Reads catalog data [PostgreSQL over TLS 1.3 with IAM Authentication]
* Order & Checkout Microservice -> Aurora Primary Writer: Reads and writes order data [PostgreSQL over TLS 1.3 with IAM Authentication]
* Recommendation Microservice -> DynamoDB & Aurora Read-Replica: Reads recommendations and cart data [AWS SDK (HTTPS) / PostgreSQL over TLS 1.3]
* Content Management & Moderation Microservice -> Aurora Primary Writer: Writes moderation data [PostgreSQL over TLS 1.3 with IAM Authentication]
* Data Stores -> AWS KMS: Enforces encryption-at-rest, Column-Level Encryption, and cryptographic erasure [Internal AWS API]

## Technology Stack
* AWS Aurora PostgreSQL: Chosen for ACID compliance, multi-currency decimal handling, and relational catalog/order integrity.
* AWS DynamoDB: Chosen for sub-10ms key-value latency supporting recommendations and cart sessions.
* AWS KMS: Chosen for encryption-at-rest, CMK least-privilege management, and GDPR cryptographic erasure.
* TLS 1.3 & mTLS: Chosen for encrypted data-in-transit across all internal database links.
* AWS IAM Database Authentication: Chosen to eliminate static credentials in favor of short-lived tokens.

## Rationale
This architecture uses polyglot persistence to separate relational transactional workloads from high-volume NoSQL lookups, meeting the 1M MAU scalability goal. Robust security controls, including IAM auth, least-privilege RBAC, and KMS encryption, ensure full GDPR/CCPA compliance and OWASP mitigation.
